cases.sentence: Львов в ___ с поясом, в замшевых ботинках сидел на кресле и в pince-nez с синими стеклами читал книгу, стоявшую на пюпитре, осторожно на отлете держа красивою рукой до половины испеплившуюся сигару.
cases.explain: «домашнем сюртуке» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Lvov, in a house coat with a belt and in chamois leather shoes, was sitting in an armchair, and with a pince-nez with blue glasses he was reading a book that stood on a reading desk, while in his beautiful hand he held a half-burned cigarette daintily away from him.

cases.sentence: Прекрасное, тонкое и молодое еще лицо его, которому курчавые блестящие ___ придавали еще более породистое выражение, просияло улыбкой, когда он увидел Левина.
cases.explain: «серебряные волосы» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: His handsome, delicate, and still youthful-looking face, to which his curly, glistening silvery hair gave a still more aristocratic air, lighted up with a smile when he saw Levin.

cases.sentence: Садитесь сюда, спокойнее… – Он встал и подвинул качалку. – Читали ___ в «Journal de St. – Petersbourg»?
cases.explain: «последний циркуляр» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Capital! I was meaning to send to you. How’s Kitty? Sit here, it’s more comfortable.” He got up and pushed up a rocking chair. “Have you read the last circular in the Journal de St. Pétersbourg? I think it’s excellent,” he said, with a slight French accent.

cases.sentence: Я нахожу прекрасно, – сказал он с несколько ___.
cases.explain: «французским акцентом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Capital! I was meaning to send to you. How’s Kitty? Sit here, it’s more comfortable.” He got up and pushed up a rocking chair. “Have you read the last circular in the Journal de St. Pétersbourg? I think it’s excellent,” he said, with a slight French accent.

cases.sentence: И,разговорившись, как обыкновенно, тотчас же перешел на более удобный ему ___. – Правда, что мне и некогда.
cases.explain: «французский язык» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “That’s what I envy you, that you are able to mix in these interesting scientific circles,” he said. And as he talked, he passed as usual into French, which was easier to him. “It’s true I haven’t the time for it. My official work and the children leave me no time; and then I’m not ashamed to own that my education has been too defective.”

cases.explain: «способные дети» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “You’ll catch all that up. They’re such clever children. The great thing is the education of character. That’s what I learn when I look at your children.”

cases.explain: «нравственное воспитание» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “You’ll catch all that up. They’re such clever children. The great thing is the education of character. That’s what I learn when I look at your children.”

cases.sentence: Так как мужу надо было ехать встречать кого-то по службе, а жене в концерт и публичное заседание ___, то надо было много решить и обдумать.
cases.explain: «юго-восточного комитета» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: And the husband and wife began to discuss their arrangements for the day. As the husband had to drive to meet someone on official business, while the wife had to go to the concert and some public meeting of a committee on the Eastern Question, there was a great deal to consider and settle. Levin had to take part in their plans as one of themselves. It was settled that Levin should go with Natalia to the concert and the meeting, and that from there they should send the carriage to the office for Arseny, and he should call for her and take her to Kitty’s; or that, if he had not finished his work, he should send the carriage back and Levin would go with her.

cases.sentence: – Нет, крайность ни в чем не хороша, – спокойно сказала Натали, укладывая его ___ на стол в определенное место.
cases.explain: «разрезной ножик» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “No, extremes are not good in anything,” Natalia said serenely, putting his paper-knife straight in its proper place on the table.

cases.sentence: – Так я же нападу на него, – улыбаясь, сказала Львова, дожидавшаяся конца разговора в своей белой ___. – Ну, поедемте.
cases.explain: «собачьей ротонде» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Well, then, I will attack him,” said Madame Lvova, with a smile, standing in her white sheepskin cape, waiting till they had finished speaking. “Come, let us go.”
